sources.note: Per search-engine summary of the entry (page itself could not be reached by automated download to scripts): Middle Persian versification was based on stress rather than syllable quantity, with a variable number of syllables per line within fixed limits; Sasanian-period verse unrhymed. The entry is about verse prosody (accentual metre), which presupposes a stress accent; it is not a description of lexical tone.

tone.quote: He suggests that the stresses or beats (ictus) which define the rhythm of a verse always fall on heavy syllables. Analysis of the intact verses of the Manichean hymn cycles supports the following rules: (1) The stress often coincides with the accent on the word, but not always. We may suppose that the accent and the stress are characterized by different phonetic properties, for instance the accent by a higher pitch and the stress by an intensity or a length.

tone.quote: 2.1.2. Предполагается силовое ударение на исходе словоформы. Безударны: энклитические личные местоимения ед. числа с кратким гласным (во мн. числе показатель -ān, вероятно, имел дополнительное ударение); неопределенный артикль -ē(v); относительная частица ī; большинство односложных предлогов и союзов, не сопровождаемых энклитическим личным местоимением; эмфатическая частица -iz. Отрицательная (nē) и запретительная (mā) частицы ударны. Долгота имеет фонологический характер.
tone.translation: 2.1.2. A dynamic (force/expiratory) stress on the final syllable of the word form is assumed. Unstressed are: the singular enclitic personal pronouns with a short vowel (in the plural the marker -ān probably bore an additional stress); the indefinite article -ē(w); the relative particle ī; most monosyllabic prepositions and conjunctions not accompanied by an enclitic personal pronoun; the emphatic particle -iz. The negative (nē) and prohibitive (mā) particles are stressed. Length is phonological.
tone.n_tones: None: dynamic (stress) accent, no tones described
